title: Rolen Ofandrus
dek: A craftsman, exacting teacher and early militia organizer who brings companions out of the mine, prepares Pristinia’s volunteers and later returns looking for pupils whose names have faded from the town’s newer company.

facts.Early role: Range owner · bow and arrow maker
facts.Last recovered expedition: 24 Sep 2024 · selected quest posting record; later status unresolved

body:
Rolen Ofandrus arrives offering help, puts a range into working order and expects the people he leads to prepare and listen. He welcomes friends warmly, gives orders sharply and later returns to Pristinia looking for pupils whose names the newer adventurers do not recognize.

Rolen makes the range usable

In March 2024, Rolen remodels and cleans the range while preparing bows, crossbows and arrows for business. He identifies himself to Pilanas Cristias as its owner and describes training and practice as its purpose. His work makes a place where equipment, instruction and a welcoming first conversation meet.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4.

Pilanas learns the craft

Pilanas asks to learn woodworking. Rolen warns that shaping good arrow shafts takes years of practice, then offers a useful starting task: attaching heads to shafts he has prepared. When she hears condescension in his explanation, he clarifies that he meant the task is easier, not that she is incapable. He demonstrates the glue and fitting process, leaving further instruction open. Craft is passed through patient work rather than a promise of instant mastery.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

Learning to protect oneself

Claire Hearthford brings Kathie to learn self-defense. Rolen presents a carved training bow, adjusts the trainees’ technique and encourages them after misses. Claire tells Kathie to attend to posture, aim and breathing instead of the target alone. Jako’s account explicitly credits Rolen’s encouragement with easing frustration and improving a shot. The range serves families and newcomers as well as experienced adventurers.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

His later status is not established by this early range history. Read the town’s wider militia record.

A building needs workers as well as bows

Before the range opens, Rolen plans practice lanes, a place for spellwork and space to sell equipment. Melian can spare some labor but asks for a written plan. Rolen writes down the stone he needs and pays a runner, then takes the boy’s suggestion about local materials seriously. When the boy wants a bow and lessons, Rolen offers an exchange: a regular supply of wood for instruction.

John asks him to help train the town’s recruits. They discuss how a small workforce must cover the quarry, farms and militia, and Rolen agrees to take willing pupils under his wing. His range grows through these arrangements with other people. Neither the supplies nor the volunteers are an unlimited resource.

The recovery he plans, and the people brought out

For the return to the fatal mine, Rolen says he has consulted Nienna and Gartina. He asks for obedience, assigns the stealth work to himself and Claire, and gives recovering the fallen priority over further exploration. The search for the missing workers is conditional on that first task going well. He restricts magic because of what the survivors reported, while admitting uncertainty about whether a companion’s natural magic could draw danger.

Pressed about command, he says Melian entrusted him with the mission and describes millennia of warfare and service to Wood Elf queens. These are his statements about his earlier life. The outcome of this expedition is firmer: after the company’s fighting, the narrator confirms that Rolen and Claire enter quietly, retrieve the bodies and find the missing companions nearby. The company then carries the dead back to town.

At the later celebration, Jako credits Rolen with leading the recovery. Rolen reassures Gartina that nobody expected her to return to the place that frightened her, and says that they lost nobody else. He also advertises the newly opened range, welcomes Alyhotep and dances with Chrissy. The same evening makes room for relief, work and pleasure after the rescue.

A warm greeting, then the commanding voice

Rolen’s militia exercises use the adventurers’ varied abilities to test the volunteers. He wants them to learn cooperation and adapt to unfamiliar attacks. At a later session he greets his friends with evident warmth, but calls them back to the purpose of the gathering when the conversation wanders. There will be another time for catching up; now they are there to train.

He expects the adventurers to take their opponents seriously and begins the exercise with named trainees whose skills differ. When time runs out, he calls it a better match than the earlier one while insisting the volunteers still need practice. His encouragement at the family range and his demanding voice before a drill belong to the same teacher.

Horses, strained tempers and burial prayers

Rolen joins the effort to secure horses for cavalry, hauling and construction, willing to contribute his own money. In the tavern he jokes that hard labor might improve Scout Lilian’s troubles with her husband, then sharply reminds her that he needs his best scout attentive. His concern and his habit of command do not always make him tactful.

On the fog-bound journey he and Lilian cover the flanks. He defers to Cobble and Vigr in the harbor’s tavern, nudges them toward a bribe and eventually threatens a contact against giving false information. A later fight brings him back to the others with his crossbow. He uses what healing he has for Kyle, explicitly says when it is exhausted, and gives the dead ranchers an Elvish burial prayer.

The encounter leaves him more urgent about fortifying and training Pristinia. This journey records bargaining, danger and care for the dead; it does not make every intended purchase or cavalry plan a completed institution.

The names nobody answers

When Rolen returns to the record in the Month of Nuru, Year 1, he expects to meet former companions and pupils. Instead he is greeted by adventurers who largely do not know him. He introduces himself as an early arrival and mentor, asks after Gartina and begins listing the wanderers he trained. His face falls; he sinks to his knees as name after name draws no recognition.

Rolen concludes that they must be gone. Eugene’s divination brings no promise of their return, and Rolen hopes they are in a better place. These are the grief and conclusions voiced in the meeting, not independent death records for every person named. Wren tells him that other old friends are in danger in Gael and presses him to help the living.

He does not know Gael. His months of travel on the Shadow Roads have brought him back seeking help with their worsening dangers, rather than a ready route to the company’s destination. He agrees to look for a way forward after they investigate the disturbance. His experience opens a possibility, but the people gathering around him have urgent purposes of their own.

A guide who has to bring them back

Rolen leads the party into the Shadow Roads after warning that his familiar route has become more dangerous. When a creature threatens them, he tries to hold its attention, then takes Eugene’s hand and drags him toward shelter. In the enclosed refuge he keeps people away from the door and uses touch and gestures to steady companions who cannot see.

An opening eventually returns the company safely to Pristinia. Rolen makes sure they go through. The danger has forced a return rather than delivered them to the disturbance he meant to investigate. When the party gathers again on a later posting date, he acknowledges that they had still been hours, perhaps a day, away.

He is willing to continue with a guide connected to Wren’s patron and speaks pointedly about greater competence than his own. The later journey finds him present again, not a proven master of every destination the Roads might reach. His final status beyond these selected autumn scenes remains unrecovered.

profile.personality: A warm host and exacting commander. At the range he corrects misunderstanding patiently; before missions he demands attention and obedience. Threats, tactless jokes and frustration remain beside his concern for the injured and missing.
profile.achievements: Helps reopen Eovar’s road, builds the Archery Range, teaches craft and family self-defense, leads the recovery of mine bodies and missing companions, trains the militia, seeks horses, investigates the fog road, answers Eovar’s warning and helps fortify Pristinia. His later Shadow Roads expedition ends in a safe return before the intended disturbance is reached; he joins the next journey without claiming mastery of it.
profile.relationships: Cobble and Vigr recur in early defense work. John helps divide scarce workers between farming, quarrying and militia; Claire shares the mine infiltration. Quake, Elenia, Adelia, Alyhotep and Loistava join teams he coordinates. Lilian scouts with him, Gartina remembers the mine’s terror, and newer companions meet his grief for the wanderers he once trained.
